sample_tweets.text: [미국 내전 초읽기 들어갔냐? 흩어진 떡밥 모아보니까 닭살 돋네 ㄷㄷ.txt](초장문주의)  미국 뉴스 맨날 파편으로만 보니까 "뭔 헛소리냐" 싶지?  선거 개판 오분 전 터진 거, 중공 공작망 털리는 거,   마두로 대가리 딴 거,   심지어 펜타곤이 하루에 시체 2,400구 묻는 훈련 돌린 것까지…  언론 새끼들은 전부 개별 사건인 척 입 꾹 닫고 있는데, 이거 타임라인 한 줄로 꿰어 맞추면 진짜 숨 막히는 그림 하나 나온다.  트럼프가 ‘외국 적대 세력 + 국내 간첩망 + 불체자 선거 주작 카르텔’을 통째로 묶어서 국가안보 위협 때리고 합법적 군사 계엄/대숙청 각 재고 있다는 가설이다.  물론 대놓고 "군대 진격!" 이러는 증거는 아직 없다.  근데 팩트랑 뇌피셜 싹 발라내고 "만약 이게 진짜면 어떻게 굴러가는지" 시나리오 돌려보면 소름 돋음.  차근차근 팩트 체크하면서 썰 풀어본다.  1. 트럼프의 빌드업: 범죄 조직 = '외국 침략군' 프레임 세팅  트럼프가 베네수엘라 갱단 '트렌 데 아라과(TdA)' 조지려고 꺼내 든 카드가 뭐냐?  무려 1798년에 만든 적성국인법(Alien Enemies Act)이다. 이게 왜 미친 짓이냐면, 이건 잡범들 추방하는 출입국관리법 따위가 아님.  선전포고 떴거나 외국 군대가 침략했을 때 적국 국민들 영장 없이 잡아 가두고 내쫓는 ‘전시 법률’임.  이걸 남미 갱단한테 꽂아버렸다는 건, 연방정부가 얘네를 단순 깡패가 아니라 "미국 본토를 무력 침략한 적국 정규군" 취급하겠다는 선언임.  대법원이 "아무리 그래도 판사 면상은 보게 해줘라(인신보호청원)" 하면서 제동을 걸긴 했음.  근데 본질은 뭐다?   행정부가 이미 헌정사 유례없는 전시 특별법을 민간 영역에 꽂아 넣을 준비를 끝마쳤다는 거임.  2. 남미 작살내기: 마두로는 이미 헬기 태워 납치해 옴  2026년 1월 3일, 미 특수부대가 카라카스 번개같이 쳐들어가서 마두로 부부 목덜미 잡고 압송해 옴.  죄목? 마약 테러(Narco-terrorism). 국제법이고 지랄이고, 미국에 펜타닐/코카인 뿌리는 배후 정권 대가리를 진짜 군사작전으로 날려버린 선례를 박아버림.  그럼 멕시코 카르텔은 안전할까?  트럼프는 이미 멕시코 카르텔도 공식 테러 조직(FTO)으로 못 박았음.  남미 마약 카르텔 - 국경 밀입국 조직 - 본토 갱단으로 이어지는 라인이 단순 밀수가 아니라 "외국 적대 세력의 비정규전 침투"로 엮이는 순간, 국방부랑 특수작전사령부(SOCOM) 움직일 명분은 100% 충족됨.  근데 여기에 '선거'가 묻으면 판이 차원이 다르게 커진다.  3. 선거판 2,028만 명 증발 사태 (SCIF 폭로 떡밥)  여기서 인터넷 뒤흔든 2026 중간선거 수치 하나 보고 가자.  2022년: 공화 5,420만 vs 민주 5,130만  2026년: 공화 5,560만(+140만) vs 민주 7,040만(+1,910만)  SCIF 쪽에서 깐 데이터 보면, 2022~2026년 사이에 각 주에서 시민권 확인 없이 불법 등록된 유권자 추정치가 딱 20,283,937명임.  민주당이 갑자기 허공에서 소환한 1,910만 표랑 귀신같이 아다리가 맞아떨어짐.  가정해보자.   저 2,000만 명이 진짜 불체자/비시민권자 표로 밀어 넣은 거라면?  이건 선거 부정이 아니라 국가 체제 전복 쿠데타임.  4. 표를 조작하는 알고리즘? 1표 = 1.25표 마법  단순 머릿수 채우기뿐만이 아님.  2000년대 초반 클린턴 커티스가 폭로했던 ‘51:49 가중치 알고리즘’ 떡밥이 다시 수면 위로 올라옴.  1인 1표가 아니라 시스템 내부에서 민주당 표에 1.25배 가중치 주고, 공화당 표는 0.75배로 깎아먹는 스크립트.  캘리포니아 전역에서 거의 동일한 비율(53:46)로 선거 결과가 찍혀 나오거나,   특정 정당에 15% 밴드가 일정하게 얹어지는 그래프가 도는 이유가 이거라는 주장임.  작업 끝나면 스스로 코드 지워버리는 자폭 스크립트라 일반 감사로는 절대 안 잡힌다는 게 호사가들 설명임.  만약 이 백도어 코드 포렌식 기록이랑 지휘 라인이 적발된다?  그때부턴 단순 투표 무효 소송이 아니라 연방 내란죄 수사로 급발진함.  5. 송도 A-WEB과 중공 커넥션: 글로벌 본진 털기  더글라스 프랭크 박사가 한국 투표소 돌고 라스베이거스랑 팟캐스트에서 대놓고 터뜨린 핵심:  "한국만 털린 게 아니다. 인천 송도에 있는 A-WEB(세계선거기관협의회)이 디지털 개표 시스템을 전 세계에 팔아치우는 글로벌 카르텔 허브다."  중국산 위조 용지, 해킹 장비, 소로스계 자금망이 한국의 인프라를 위장 기지로 써먹었다는 의혹임.  A-WEB 시스템 자체는 망분리되어 있다고 선관위가 펄쩍 뛰지만, 미국 정보기관(NSA/사이버사령부) 시각에서 "외국 세력이 선거 인프라를 플랫폼화해서 동맹국과 미국 본토를 교란했다"는 그림으로 넘어가면 이건 외교 문제가 아니라 방첩/군사 작전 영역이 됨.  6. 행정명령 13848호: 합법적 대청소 스위치  트럼프가 1기 때 박아두고 이번에 비상사태 또 연장해 둔 치트키가 바로 행정명령 13848호임.  선거 끝나고 45일 안에 DNI(국가정보국)가 '외국 선거 개입 보고서'를 대통령 책상에 직보하게 되어 있음.  불법 등록 2,000만 명  전자개표 가중치 알고리즘  중공/해외 자금 및 기술 지원  이 3개가 보고서 한 장으로 묶여 올라가는 순간?  금융 제재, 계좌 동결, 국가비상사태 발동까지 법적으로 락이 풀림.  다만 이 명령 하나로 군대를 곧장 투입할 순 없음. (미국엔 민간 치안에 군 투입을 금지하는 포시 코미타투스법이 버티고 있으니까.)  하지만 합법적 사법망으로 목줄을 죄기엔 차고 넘침.  7. 주 정부 vs 연방 보안관: 내전의 현실적 뇌관  메릴랜드 하포드 카운티 제프리 갈러 보안관 사건 봤지?  레이첼 모린, 케일라 해밀턴이 불체자 손에 잔인하게 찢겨 죽었는데, 민주당 주 정부는 "287(g) 공조 끊어라, 불체자 잡지 마라"고 지랄함.  빡친 보안관 18명이 주 정부 상대로 위헌 소송 박아버림. 이게 뭘 뜻하냐?  연방정부가 불체자·불법투표 전수조사 칼 빼들었을 때, 캘리포니아나 뉴욕 같은 블루 스테이트(민주당 주)는 "우린 협조 안 해, 연방 요원 꺼져" 하면서 주 경찰 동원해 막아설 거라는 거임.  지방 권력(주정부)과 중앙 권력(연방정부)의 물리적 충돌. 내전의 시작은 항상 이런 법 집행 충돌에서 터졌음.  8. 네빌 싱엄과 중공의 자금 침투  상하이에 거주하는 거물 IT 사업가 네빌 로이 싱엄(Neville Roy Singham).  미 하원 청문회에서 애나 파울리나 루나 의원이 대놓고 깠음. 싱엄의 수억 달러 검은돈이 극좌 마르크스주의 조직(PSL)과 미국민주사회주의자(DSA) 하부망으로 들어가서 반미 시위와 체제 전복 여론전을 조종하고 있다는 정황.  외국의 적성국(중공) 돈을 받아 미국 정치판을 흔들었다?   외국대리인등록법(FARA) 위반 수준을 넘어 간첩법(Espionage Act) 적용각임.  9. 펜타곤 청문회: 슬로킨의 발작과 헤그세스의 포커페이스  미시간 민주당 엘리사 슬로킨(전직 CIA) 의원이 국방장관 지명자 피트 헤그세스 청문회에서 왜 그렇게 표독스럽게 물고 늘어졌겠냐?  "트럼프가 군대 보내서 투표함 압수하라고 하면 따를 거냐, 거부할 거냐? 각서 써라." 헤그세스 답변?  "함정 질문 안 받음 ㅋ 불법적인 명령은 안 따름."  원론적인 답변만 던지고 끝까지 군 불개입 각서를 안 써줌.  민주당도 알고 있는 거임. 만약 사태가 걷잡을 수 없이 터지면, 트럼프가 '반란법(Insurrection Act)'을 켜서 군대를 시내 한복판에 들이밀 수도 있다는 악몽을.  10. 미군의 하루 2,400구 매장 훈련 (Dragon Covenant)  제일 소름 돋는 떡밥.  2026년 10월, 미 육군 제3원정지원사령부가 노스캐롤라이나에서 극비리에 친 훈련: '드래곤 커버넌트(Operation Dragon Covenant)'.  D6 불도저 밀어 넣어서 참호 파고, 공병중대 풀가동해서 하루 최대 2,400구 시신을 임시 매장하는 작전 절차를 실사 검증함.  미군 피셜로는 "중국·러시아 같은 적성국과의 대규모 정규전(Peer adversary) 대비 전사자 수습 훈련"이라고 선을 그었음.  맞아, 공식 목적은 해외 전면전 대비임.  근데 미국 본토의 정치적 내전 위기설이 극에 달한 타이밍에 하필 미군이 '대량 사상자 매장' 데이터를 뽑았다는 사실 자체가 온갖 밀덕과 음모론자들 회로를 불타오르게 만드는 거임. 결론: 방아쇠는 이미 당겨졌는가?  사건들을 한 줄로 세워보자.  트럼프는 남미 카르텔을 '외국 침략 세력'으로 규정해 적성국인법을 켰다.  마두로를 군사력으로 납치하며 국경 밖 무력 사용 선례를 남겼다.  중공 자금망(싱엄)과 글로벌 선거 인프라(A-WEB) 의혹을 안보 위협으로 몰아가고 있다.  행정명령 13848호로 외국 개입 규명 시 전산·자산 동결 명분을 쥐고 있다.  중간선거 2,028만 표 조작 의혹과 알고리즘 떡밥이 뇌관으로 대기 중이다.  주 정부와 연방 보안관들은 이미 이민·치안 문제로 총성 없는 전쟁 중이다.  미군은 전면전에 준하는 대량 전사자 수습 능력을 점검했다. 이게 하나의 거대한 비밀 작전이라는 증거는 없음.  하지만 만약 저 불법 투표와 전산 조작이 연방법원이나 특별검사 손에서 '실제 증거'로 까발려지는 순간?  연방정부의 체포 작전 개시 ➔ 블루 스테이트 주지사들의 연방 명령 거부 및 주방위군 대치 ➔ 거리의 안티파 vs 극우 무장 민병대 총격전 ➔ 대통령의 반란법 발동 및 군 병력 투입.  현대 미국의 내전은 남북전쟁처럼 대포 쏘면서 시작하지 않는다.  "부정선거 카르텔 척결"이라는 국가안보의 이름과, "파시즘 군사 쿠데타 저지"라는 민주주의의 이름이 정면으로 들이받는 순간 터지는 거임.  진짜 팝콘각은 이제부터다. 실시간 기소장이랑 군 통수권 움직임 똑바로 지켜봐라. ---------------------------------------------------------- [Connecting the red string: Tren de Aragua, 20M ghost voters, Singham’s CCP cash, and the Army digging 2,400 graves a day. Is America setting the board for a domestic flashpoint? ]  Look, if you consume cable news, every headline looks like a random, disconnected clown show.  Tren de Aragua running wild in apartment complexes.  DHS threatening to audit voter rolls. Elissa Slotkin sweating bullets in defense hearings. Maduro getting bagged in Caracas. The Army out in North Carolina running drills on how fast they can bulldozer mass graves. The media wants you to treat these as isolated incidents. But if you step back and look at the actual statutory instruments being dusted off, the legal precedents being set, and the raw panic in the establishment, a terrifying picture emerges:  The executive branch isn't just fighting culture wars—they are methodically building the legal and military framework to treat the domestic opposition apparatus, foreign dark money, and transnational cartels as a single, unified hostile foreign force on U.S. soil.  Is this an actual coordinated master plan, or just an unhinged storm of post-election chaos colliding with institutional decay? Let’s lay out the receipts, separate the confirmed facts from the fringe intel, and look at where this trajectory actually leads.  1. The Precedent: Transnational Gangs as "Invading Armies"  Trump didn't just vow to deport illegal immigrants; he dusted off the Alien Enemies Act of 1798 against Tren de Aragua (TdA).  Why does this matter? The AEA isn't standard immigration law (Title 8). It’s an explicit wartime statute intended for declared wars or predatory foreign invasions. By invoking it, the administration attempted to categorize criminal street cartels not as domestic perps entitled to standard civil proceedings, but as foreign hostile combatants.  Sure, SCOTUS stepped in (Trump v. J.G.G.) and reminded the executive that habeas corpus still exists—detainees still get notice and a day in court. But the cat is out of the bag: the White House has actively tested the waters of treating cross-border crime as a literal military invasion of the homeland.  2. Kinetic Precedents: The Maduro Snatch  On January 3, 2026, U.S. special operations went kinetic in Caracas, bagging Nicolás Maduro and his wife on narco-terrorism charges.  Forget international diplomacy for a second—look at the operational doctrine. The administration officially established that foreign heads of state and cartel leaders trafficking drugs into the homeland are military targets, not diplomatic counterweights.  Apply that same logic to Mexican cartels designated as Foreign Terrorist Organizations (FTOs). If cartel foot soldiers operating inside U.S. borders are legally classified as foreign combatants operating on behalf of designated terrorist entities, Title 10 (military) and Title 50 (covert intelligence) authorities start bleeding into what used to be local police work.  3. The 20-Million Ghost Voter Hypothesis  Now factor in the election chaos. The viral claims circulating through alternative networks (SCIF et al.) highlight numbers that are fueling the rage engine:  2022: Rep 54.2M vs. Dem 51.3M  2026: Rep 55.6M (+1.4M) vs. Dem 70.4M (+19.1M)  The narrative being pushed is that roughly 20,283,937 non-citizens were illegally grandfathered into voter registries between 2022 and 2026, matching almost 1:1 with the anomalous Dem surge. While certified election data and state audits routinely debunk the notion of tens of millions of non-citizens successfully casting ballots, the perception among half the electorate is already cemented. When you have DHS leadership (Markwayne Mullin) jumping on television promising to subpoena federal voter databases, match Social Security files, and pursue felony charges against non-citizen voters, the stage is set for a historic jurisdictional brawl between red feds and blue states.  4. Algorithmic Warfare & Self-Deleting Scripts  On top of voter registration numbers, the ghost of Clinton Curtis (the programmer who testified before Congress in the 2000s about fractional voting algorithms) has resurfaced.  The claim: modern voting systems aren't running 1:1 vote tallies, but using weighted percentages (e.g., 1 Dem vote = 1.25; 1 GOP vote = 0.75), engineered with self-scrubbing zero-footprint scripts that evade routine post-election audits. Critics point to identical 53–46 margin bands in contested districts as circumstantial proof.  Whether it's genuine statistical noise or malicious code, if an administrative forensic team claims to find hard evidence of code-level manipulation, it immediately escalates from a routine recount dispute into a Title 18 sedition and treason investigation.  5. The A-WEB Node & The Foreign Nexus  Enter the international angle. Voices like Dr. Douglas G. Frank have been zeroing in on A-WEB (Association of World Election Bodies), headquartered in Songdo, South Korea.  The working theory: A-WEB isn't just an innocent NGO doing election monitoring in developing democracies; it's a clearinghouse for centralized electronic voting architectures susceptible to CCP backdoors and transnational NGO funding. Combine that with Peter Schweizer’s warnings in The Invisible Coup, and the narrative pivots: American elections aren't just being contested by rival domestic parties—they’re being sabotaged by an international nexus of Chinese cyber assets, Soros-funded NGOs, and compromised hardware.  6. The Loaded Gun: Executive Order 13848  Remember Trump’s 2018 Executive Order 13848? The one mandating a DNI assessment within 45 days of an election to identify foreign interference, backed by emergency asset freezes? It was quietly renewed and kept operational.  If DNI, NSA, and USCYBERCOM drop a report officially alleging that foreign state actors (CCP/Venezuela) funneled money or manipulated network infrastructure in conjunction with domestic activist groups:  The President can declare a full economic and administrative emergency.  Bank accounts of targeted organizations can be frozen without prior indictment.  The legal threshold for federal intervention shifts from "civil regulatory audit" to "national security counter-offensive." 7. Blue State Rebellion: The Sheriffs Draw the Line Look at Harford County, Maryland. Sheriff Jeffrey Gahler went to Capitol Hill, slammed the table over the brutal murders of Rachel Morin and Kayla Hamilton by illegal gang affiliates, and called out Democratic sanctuary policies to their faces. Then, 18 out of 24 Maryland sheriffs banded together to sue their own state government over sanctuary restrictions.  This is the fault line. If the federal government attempts sweeping raids, voter roll confiscations, or mass detentions, blue state governors and city councils will explicitly order state troopers and municipal police to resist or non-cooperate. What happens when an ICE/Border Patrol tactical team, backed by federal marshals, faces off against state police blocking access to a municipal building? That’s where the shooting starts.  8. Neville Roy Singham & The Chinese Dark Money Pipeline  This isn't just about street crime; it’s about elite subversion. House Republicans (like Anna Paulina Luna) have been hammering Neville Roy Singham—the Shanghai-based tech millionaire whose multi-hundred-million-dollar fortune has funded Marxist fronts, the Party for Socialism and Liberation (PSL), and radical protest infrastructure across major American metros.  If the DOJ ties street agitators, campus encampments, and anti-enforcement militias directly to Shanghai wire transfers, the administration will bypass standard political channels and start dropping Espionage Act and FARA hammers.  9. Hegseth’s Poker Face at the Pentagon  Why did Sen. Elissa Slotkin (ex-CIA) spend her confirmation hearing time relentlessly grilling Defense Secretary nominee Pete Hegseth?  "Will you follow an order to seize voting machines? Will you put troops on U.S. streets? Pledge on paper right now that you won't."  Hegseth’s response was a flat, clinical refusal to take the bait: "I will follow lawful orders, and I will not answer gotcha hypotheticals."  The establishment knows the Insurrection Act of 1807 exists. If blue cities erupt in widespread civil unrest following federal enforcement actions, the President has the statutory power to federalize the National Guard or deploy active-duty troops to suppress domestic violence and enforce federal law, overriding governors completely. 10. The Chilling Detail: Operation Dragon Covenant  Now look at the quiet logistics.  In October 2026, the 3rd Expeditionary Sustainment Command and 20th Engineer Brigade ran Operation Dragon Covenant at Fort Bragg (Liberty), NC. Using D6 bulldozers, combat engineers dug temporary burial trenches capable of holding 20 casualties every 75 minutes. The final technical takeaway? A single combat engineer company running non-stop operations could bury up to 2,400 remains per day.  The Pentagon’s official briefing makes it clear: this is for large-scale, high-intensity peer-adversary warfare (e.g., a bloody clash in the Indo-Pacific or Eastern Europe) where local air supremacy is contested and remains cannot be immediately flown home on refrigerated C-17s.  It is standard, doctrinal contingency planning. But when you look at the domestic climate—armed sheriffs suing governors, federal agencies gearing up for mass voter roll purges, foreign regimes getting decapitated, and political factions viewing each other as existential threats—the sheer optic of the military drilling 2,400-body-per-day mass internments hits like a cold slap in the face.  The Verdict: How It Actually Kicks Off  A second American Civil War will not look like 1861. You won't see blue and grey uniforms marching across Gettysburg with artillery batteries.  It will look like Northern Ireland during the Troubles combined with the collapse of the Roman Republic:  Federal Subpoenas & Raids: DOJ and DHS issue mass warrants for state voter databases and undocumented gang targets.  State Nullification: Blue governors declare the orders unconstitutional, barricade administrative offices, and deploy State Police to shield municipal infrastructure.  Street-Level Kinetics: Armed paramilitary factions (Antifa/PSL street blocks vs. constitutionalist militias/deputized posses) violently clash in suburban choke points.  The Insurrection Act: The White House invokes the Insurrection Act, federalizes the Guard, and deploys federal forces to break state resistance.  Constitutional Breakdown: Courts issue contradictory emergency stays; executive branches on both sides ignore them.  Is the country definitely doomed to this meat grinder? Not necessarily. The judiciary, military chain of command, and federalist friction are specifically engineered to slow down and diffuse this kind of kinetic spiral.  The takeaway isn't that a war is pre-scheduled on the calendar. It’s that every single systemic fail-safe—elections, the courts, the border, and federal law enforcement—is currently being redlined at maximum pressure.  Watch the federal court dockets, watch the movement of Title 10 forces, and watch who blinks first when the subpoenas hit the blue state capitals. The fuse is lit.

5. MAJOR RESCUE & EMERGENCY RESPONSE – Cooperation with Emergency Services  Safety requires not only threat detection but also an effective response.  MAJOR SHIELD should cooperate with Major Rescue and authorised emergency services.  The system could provide:  - The precise location of an incident. - The type of detected threat. - Available information about the situation on site. - Information about blocked roads and alternative access routes. - Guidance for reaching injured people safely.  This would give emergency services a more complete picture of the situation before they arrive.  6. Ethics and Privacy Protection  MAJOR SHIELD must never become a tool for mass surveillance.  Its operation should be based on several fundamental principles:  - Respect for citizens' privacy and data minimisation. - Local data processing wherever technically possible. - No profiling based on appearance, origin, beliefs or presumed intentions. - No automatic assignment of guilt. - Alert verification and human oversight of intervention decisions. - Auditable algorithms and clear accountability. - Protection against cyberattacks and misuse.  The system should protect people, not restrict their freedom without justified necessity.  7. Integration with MAJOR CARS 2.0  MAJOR SHIELD does not replace existing Major Cars functions. It extends their capabilities through cooperation with intelligent urban infrastructure.  MAJOR ALERT – Driver Fatigue Protection remains responsible for driver safety and detecting the risk of impaired driving ability. It is not intended to diagnose people or assess their intentions.  MAJOR SHIELD has a separate mission: protecting public spaces through cooperation between vehicles, infrastructure and emergency services.  Our Vision  The future of safety should not mean that everyone is constantly monitored. It should mean that intelligent technologies can recognise genuine threats early enough to prevent them or reduce their consequences.  We do not want cars that suspect people. We want cars and cities that know how to protect people.  MAJOR SHIELD – Intelligence that prevents. Technology that protects.  Safety begins before danger occurs.

MAJOR CARS 2.0 – MAJOR SHIELD  An Intelligent Public Safety and Threat Prevention System  The first version creates possibilities. The second reveals value. Every next version brings us closer to excellence.  Safety begins before danger occurs  The vision of Major Cars goes far beyond the traditional understanding of a car as a means of transportation. The intelligent vehicle of the future should cooperate with its surroundings, urban infrastructure and emergency services, creating an integrated safety ecosystem.  One element of this vision is MAJOR SHIELD – an intelligent system designed to prevent threats in public spaces.  Its primary purpose is not to identify potential criminals or judge people based on their appearance, behaviour or beliefs. Its purpose is to detect dangerous situations, limit their escalation and activate appropriate protective procedures as early as possible.  1. MAJOR SAFE ZONE – Intelligent Urban Zones  Imagine future cities where selected areas, such as public squares, pedestrian zones, schools, hospitals, railway stations and stadiums, are equipped with intelligent safety infrastructure.  MAJOR SAFE ZONE could use:  - Geofencing to define restricted traffic areas precisely. - Vehicle-to-infrastructure communication. - Automatic retractable bollards and anti-ram barriers. - Recognition of authorised emergency, service and delivery vehicles. - Monitoring of unauthorised access attempts and dangerous driving manoeuvres.  A vehicle approaching a restricted zone would receive information about the applicable access restrictions. If an unauthorised entry is attempted, the infrastructure could activate appropriate protective measures and notify the relevant authorities.  2. MAJOR SECURITY GATES – Intelligent Access Control  In locations particularly exposed to security risks, especially during mass events, intelligent access control points could be introduced.  These could combine:  - Automatic number plate recognition. - Technologies for detecting weapons and dangerous objects. - Verification of access permissions. - Physical anti-ram barriers. - Communication with urban security centres.  Detection technologies should be selected according to the specific threat. No single sensor can guarantee the detection of every type of weapon or dangerous object.  3. MAJOR SECURITY AI – Intelligent Threat Analysis  This is the central analytical component of the system.  Artificial intelligence could analyse information received from urban infrastructure, sensors and participating vehicles.  Its role would be to identify situations requiring attention, including:  - Attempts to breach security barriers. - Vehicles entering pedestrian zones at dangerous speeds. - Dangerous manoeuvres near large crowds. - Repeated attempts to gain unauthorised access. - Situations where multiple independent sensors indicate the same potential threat.  A single signal should never automatically constitute evidence of criminal intent. The system should verify information, assess the reliability of alerts and minimise false alarms.  4. MAJOR PREVENTION – Prevention Instead of Reaction  This is the philosophical and technological core of the entire solution.  Traditional security systems often focus on responding after an incident has occurred. MAJOR PREVENTION aims to move the intervention point to an earlier stage.  If an unauthorised vehicle attempts to enter a protected zone, the system should not wait for an accident or an attack to happen.  It could warn the driver, activate protective barriers, secure access to the area and notify the relevant authorities.  When a serious threat is detected, the system should enable rapid coordination of protective and emergency response procedures.

🧵  A GB News monologue by Patrick Christys turned a routine US midterm defeat into a story about Muslims, minorities, the “Islamo-left” and the decline of Western civilisation.  “Well, good evening. If you care about Western civilisation, last night was a bad night.” So began Patrick Christys’s GB News monologue on 4 November.  Democrats won the House and the Senate, flipping Senate seats in Kansas, Iowa, Texas, Ohio, Maine, North Carolina and South Carolina. Reuters reported that the scale of the gains went well beyond the usual battlegrounds into Republican territory, and that several of Trump’s own hand-picked candidates lost races the party had expected to win. Thankfully, Trump accepted the result.  A swing against the sitting president’s party is the ordinary rhythm of American politics: the governing party has lost Senate seats in 13 of the 20 midterms since 1946.  So the event being mourned by Christys, framed by him as a signifier of ‘the decline of Western civilisation’, was, in reality, a free election resulting in a shift in legislative control, and a defeated president accepting the outcome.  “Western civilisation” usually refers to the shared cultural heritage, social norms, ethical values, philosophies and political systems rooted primarily in European and Mediterranean histories, and extending to societies shaped by European migration and colonisation, such as the United States.  While its influence, meanings and timeframe are complex and contested, few would dispute that competitive elections, a legislature that checks the executive, and the peaceful transfer of power are among its most distinctive and significant achievements.  French jurist, historian, and political philosopher Montesquieu is the principal source of the theory of the separation of powers, which was a direct influence on James Madison and the American constitution. On the evidence of election night, Western institutions worked exactly as designed.  Why, then, did a GB News presenter insist it was “a bad night” for “Western civilisation”?  Part of the answer lies in how the rhetorical construction of his opening sentence works. “If you care about Western civilisation” places the verdict inside the condition. By the sentence’s own logic, a viewer who welcomed the result is someone who simply does not care about Western civilisation. This is absurd: it is perfectly reasonable to both welcome the outcome of the midterms AND care about Western civilisation. But the construction means that from then on, Christys never has to even bother to argue that the Democrats threaten the West, because disagreeing with him already counts as not caring.  George Lakoff showed how a frame, once accepted, decides which facts seem relevant before any are offered. Here the civilisation frame turns an election result into an existential threat before a single policy is mentioned. The rest of the monologue then fills that frame. And what it fills it with is revealing.  The first winner Christys turns to is Abdul El-Sayed, the new Democratic senator for Michigan. A viral clip shows him in a heated exchange with Sky News’s US correspondent James Matthews outside a polling station. Christys complains that when El-Sayed “attacks reporters he’s a hero apparently”, but when Trump “has a pop at them” he is “the bad guy”. Note the verbs: El-Sayed attacks; Trump merely has a pop.  The clash happened, and while one heated exchange is a fair target for criticism, setting it against years of attacks and aggressive personal insults on the press and individual (particularly female) journalists from the Oval Office is whataboutism: a single incident is used to neutralise a long record.  Christys then plays a clip of Ro Khanna, an Indian-American of Punjabi descent and a practising Hindu who is the Democratic congressman for California’s 17th district since 2017, just re-elected, introduced with “this guy summed up the results pretty well”. Khanna celebrates the night’s firsts: likely three black governors, the first Latina governor in Texas, the first Muslim American senator, the first gay senator. “I love this America,” he says.  Christys adds nothing to the list, and he does not need to. Played in a monologue that opened with a civilisational lament, a politician’s celebration of diversity becomes further evidence of civilisational decline. The GB News audience is trusted to hear it as bad news.  Next, as Christys puts it, comes “the obligatory celebration in a foreign language from a woman who might be deported because of an alleged dodgy marriage”. The woman is Ilhan Omar, the Minnesota congresswoman who has served since 2019, and one of the first two Muslim women elected to the U.S. Congress.  The allegations about her marriage have circulated for years, have never been proven, and she denies them. Omar is an elected representative and a naturalised US citizen, so before she could be “deported” she would first have to be stripped of her citizenship. But Christys has used her not so subtly to make a link between Muslims and deportations.  “Obligatory” and “foreign language” do rhetorical work here too. American politicians of both parties routinely speak to voters in languages other than English; Republicans from George W. Bush to Marco Rubio have campaigned in Spanish. Presented as alien is not the practice but the speaker, and an unproven allegation is attached to a sitting member of Congress with “alleged” as the only qualifier.  This is arguably the core of the segment, and Teun van Dijk’s “ideological square” explains how it works. Polarised discourse tends to emphasise THEIR bad qualities and OUR good ones, while playing down THEIR good qualities and OUR bad ones.  What the winning candidates proposed on prices, healthcare or corruption (the issues voters ranked highest) barely features in Christys’s monologue. What remains is a focus on a handful of winners and their faith, their ethnicity, their sexuality, and the language they celebrate in.  In short, Christys’s ‘evidence’ that “Western civilisation” suffered “a bad night” is the identity of a handful of cherry-picked people who won.  The sociologist Rogers Brubaker has a name for this. In a 2017 article he described a shift among Northern and Western European populists from nationalism to “civilisationism”: the nation redefined as part of a Christian, or post-Christian, West set against Islam. Brubaker noted a striking feature of that politics. Its leaders often embraced gender equality and gay rights as Western values, precisely so they could be contrasted with Muslim minorities. The GB News segment departs from that model.  By airing Khanna’s list as bad news, it places a gay senator alongside a Muslim one as symptoms of the same decline. That is closer to American religious-right traditionalism than to the liberal-sounding civilisationism of Pim Fortuyn. What unites the items on the list is that each winner falls outside an older picture of who represents the West.  The pattern continues in Texas, where James Talarico became the first Democrat to win a US Senate seat in the state since 1988. Christys plays his victory speech, in which Talarico names “the richest man in the world [Musk], the most powerful man in the world [Trump], and the entire Washington DC establishment” as his Goliaths. In response, Christys derisively and dramatically snorts that Talarico has “really managed to stretch that analogy out”.  Christys then turns to Talarico’s description of his border policy: “Our southern border should be like our front porch. There should be a giant welcome mat out front, and a lock on the door”. Talarico uses this analogy to argue that border security and welcoming legal immigration are not mutually exclusive.  Christys mocks Talarico: “Great. So what, you keep them out, but you say, well, you could come in? We’re not going to let you in, but we could, we could let you in?” That only reads as a contradiction if legal and illegal migration are treated as one and the same, which Talarico explicitly does not.  A lawful entrance and a locked door describe the immigration position of all Western democracies. Even Restore Britain, which says “far more people must leave Britain than arrive”, accepts that some migrants will arrive.  There is another insinuation along the way, too. Christys says Talarico “wanted THEM to vote for him” straight after describing Texas as a centre of illegal immigration. The implication is that undocumented migrants are part of the electorate. They are not. Only US citizens can vote in federal elections, and the extremely rare cases of illegal voting by non-citizens are criminal offences.  Then comes a clip of Darializa Avila Chevalier, the community organiser backed by the Democratic Socialists of America who unseated Adriano Espaillat in a Harlem primary and has now been elected to the House. A convert to Islam in recent years, she is the first Dominican-American woman elected to Congress. Behind her in the clip GB News offer are placards reading “Tax the rich” and “Babies not bombs”.  “Apparently, she wants to defund all police. Have absolutely no border,” Christys says, and her main issue “appears to be Gaza”. Here he has at least some documented basis. CNN’s KFile team reviewed archived posts from her deleted Twitter account, dating from 2018 to 2022, which included calls to abolish police, prisons and borders; she has said they do not reflect who she is today.  Christys is less keen on scrutiny when it points the other way. In an interview the same week, he described undercover investigations into Reform UK, led by fellow GB News presenter Nigel Farage, as an attempt “to knock Reform out and knock Nigel Farage out before there’s even an election”, though he conceded some of what they found was “beyond the pale”.  Anyone’s politics are fair game for criticism. But what the segment does with them is another matter. One socialist in a safe New York seat becomes evidence that the West is falling. Christys never mentions her faith; here, it is her stance on Gaza that he uses to place her among the “Islamo-left”. “And who does that remind you of?” Christys then asks, cutting to a clip of Mothin Ali, the British Muslim Leeds councillor who is now the Green Party’s deputy leader, and then to footage from Birmingham.  On 3 November Birmingham City Council voted 54 to 19 for a six-month review of its own and the West Midlands Pension Fund’s Israel-linked investments, with options including divestment, and the clip shows councillors chanting “Free Palestine” as it passed. “It’s just pathetic, isn’t it?” Christys says. “The West is falling.”  Later he concludes: “It looks like the Islamo-left is on the march here in Britain and over in the United States as well.”  The phrase “Islamo-left” is an import. It translates the French islamo-gauchisme, a term the writer Pierre-André Taguieff says he coined in the early 2000s, first used in print in his 2002 book La Nouvelle Judéophobie, and taken up by Emmanuel Macron’s ministers in 2020 and 2021. When the higher education minister asked France’s national research body, the CNRS, to investigate it, the CNRS replied in a statement on 17 February 2021 that it was a political slogan corresponding to no scientific reality.  Its usefulness to the right lies elsewhere. It merges very different people and causes into one enemy: a Muslim senator in Michigan, a socialist in Harlem, the Green Party’s deputy leader, and a council vote in Birmingham. “On the march” completes the picture with the image of an advancing army. The segment’s YouTube title, “ISLAMO-LEFTISM SWEEPS AMERICA”, shows this was the channel’s framing as well as the presenter’s.  Perhaps the most telling moment comes when the programme plays clips of the Prime Minister reflecting on the midterm results. The clip shows Andy Burnham opening with “President Trump has accepted the results” and reading the outcome primarily as a vote about the cost of living, made worse by conflict in the Middle East and Russia’s war in Ukraine.  GB News edited out the middle of his statement, in which Burnham said these were the main things to focus on, that he would be asking leaders to do so in his calls, and that people wanted to see the world coming together on the things that matter to them. The cut removed his call for international cooperation.  There is an irony here. GB News gave extensive critical coverage to the BBC’s Panorama edit of Trump’s 6 January 2021 speech, which spliced together passages almost an hour apart and is now the subject of Trump’s $10bn lawsuit. The two edits are not equivalent: Panorama’s created a false impression of incitement, while this one removed a passage. But part of the BBC’s admitted failure was cutting a speech without making the edit clear to viewers. GB News did the same.  Having played the edited clip of Burnham, Christys said that he is “struggling to take anything that guy says seriously”. The segment then cuts to footage of Burnham and Ed Miliband playing steel drums, followed by Christys saying “Good grief”. Ridicule often stands in for analysis on GB News. As the segment’s own footage contradicts the unhinged idea that “the West is falling”, Christys moves on.  US voters themselves agree with Burnham. In the AP Voter Poll, a survey of the midterm electorate conducted by SSRS for AP, Fox News, CNN and other networks, 39% named the economy as the most important issue facing the country and 33% the state of democracy. Immigration was named by just 14%. Nor was this a vote by minorities alone.  Among white voters, 41% said one reason for their House vote was to express opposition to Trump, against 18% who said it was to express support. In rural areas and small towns the figures were 33% and 22%; among voters without a college degree, 38% and 21%.  Others who agreed with Burnham’s analysis include the two right-leaning members of Christys’s own panel discussion following his monologue.  Mark Littlewood, former director general of the Institute of Economic Affairs (IEA), shared Christys’s alarm about what he called the “fruit cake left”, but told him he was “a little bit more optimistic” than the monologue implied: Trump had promised no more wars and falling prices, voters had not got them, and so they voted the other way.  Another regular panellist, right-wing pub landlord Adam Brooks, called it a protest vote over what Trump had done with Iran and “how it has affected them in their pockets”, adding that his handling of the Epstein files had not helped. Brooks expected those voters to return once they had seen “the damage that the left can cause”, but his explanation for the result was the war, prices, and Trump’s own record.  So both of Christys’s right-leaning guests gave the conventional explanation he had disparaged just a few minutes before when it came from Burnham.  The sharpest exchange came when the journalist Nina Myskow challenged the focus on El-Sayed. When asked what proportion of Americans are Muslim, Adam Brooks offered 1.5% of the US population; Myskow corrected him to 1.6%. But Mark Littlewood then shifted the ground: “So it’s not the fact that he’s a Muslim that troubles me. It’s that the Democrat party is deserting or at least moving away from the moderate ground.”  As a former head of the IEA, and a central figure in the Tufton Street free-market network, Littlewood is hardly a moderate himself. As IEA director-general he strongly praised Truss and Kwarteng’s September 2022 mini-budget at the time, calling it a refreshing pro-growth “boost-up” package, welcoming the tax cuts and deregulation, and describing himself as “bowled over”. He and the IEA were widely seen as a key intellectual influence behind Trussonomics.  His sudden shift away from the focus on Muslims to the Democratic party “moving away from the moderate ground” demonstrates a rhetorical pattern which the philosopher Nicholas Shackel named the “motte-and-bailey” fallacy, also called the castle and courtyard.  A bold, contentious claim (the bailey) is advanced (e.g. Muslims being democratically elected is a sign of Western civilisation collapsing); when it is challenged, a modest, defensible one (the motte) is offered in its place (e.g. Democrats are moving away from a more moderate position), and the bold claim returns once the challenge has passed.  Here the two halves came from different voices. The bailey was Christys’s: a monologue and a closing line that foreground religion. The motte was Littlewood’s: ordinary opposition to the ‘immoderate’ left. The bold claim duly returned, since the clip GB News published on YouTube still carries the title “ISLAMO-LEFTISM SWEEPS AMERICA”. If the ‘immoderate’ left was the real concern, the segment had no need to begin with a Muslim senator.  There is a regulatory reason for the panel, too. @Ofcom’s Broadcast Code allows presenters of current affairs programmes like Christys’ to give their own views on political controversies, provided alternative viewpoints are adequately represented. Nina Myskow, the lone dissenting voice, is presumably how GB News would say it met that test. Earlier this year, Ofcom received 3,815 complaints in a single week about the programme’s 6 February edition, after Christys’s comments about grooming gangs and Eid. No breach has been reported.  Chas Critcher’s work on moral panics is helpful here too. He lists disproportionality among the key attributes of a panic: a reaction out of all proportion to the actual threat. A partial fit is enough to make the concept useful here.  A midterm swing against a sitting president, on a night when the loser conceded and power was due to pass under constitutional rules, is narrated as civilisational collapse, with Muslims, gays, other minorities and the left cast as the agents. That matches the wider vocabulary of GB News. Co-owner Sir Paul Marshall has urged audiences to “recover confidence in our civilisation and defend it from parasitic and progressive follies”.  So what, precisely, was the evidence presented to support the decline of Western civilisation narrative and framing on election night? The elections, the counting and the concession all held. The courts and Congress will go on checking the president. What Christys really mourned was the result, and some of the people it put in office.  Christys and those like him claim to be defending Western civilisation. But a civilisation defined by who wins a democratic election is a pretty fucking narrow thing to defend, and a very long way from the tradition of Montesquieu and Madison.

AI 해킹 도구 Artex의 공개 배포본 800개 이상이 비밀번호 없이 인터넷에 노출됐다.  더 심각한 점은 이 도구가 이미 한국 금융권 공격에 사용된 전례가 있다는 것이다.  Censys가 11월 5일 공개한 조사에 따르면 인터넷에서 발견된 Artex 콘솔은 1,465개. 동일한 호스팅 설정으로 중복된 사례를 제외하면 독립적인 배포본은 약 815개로 추정된다.  Artex는 AI 에이전트가 공격 목표를 분석하고 작업을 나눈 뒤, 취약점 탐색과 실행을 반복하는 자율 침투 테스트 도구다. Microsoft는 정찰부터 데이터 유출까지 사람의 개입을 최소화해 수행할 수 있다고 설명했다.  실제 공격 사례도 있다.  CrowdStrike는 9월 말부터 10월 초까지 한국 금융기관을 겨냥한 공격에서 Artex가 사용됐다고 밝혔다. 한 은행의 대출 조회 서비스와 다른 은행의 직원 모바일 시스템이 침해됐고, 데이터 유출도 확인됐다.  Censys는 해당 공격자의 서버에서 한국 은행뿐 아니라 결제·게임 서비스 관련 공격 데이터도 발견했다.  더 흥미로운 부분은 공격자의 보안 실수다. Artex 서버 32곳에서 공개 디렉터리가 발견됐고, 일부에는 침투 도구와 악성코드, 공격 작업 기록까지 남아 있었다.  AI가 공격을 자동화해도 운영자의 보안 실수까지 없애주지는 않는다.  공격 도구가 공개된 것과 외부인이 무단으로 공격을 실행할 수 있다는 것은 별개지만, 이미 실제 공격에 사용된 도구가 이렇게 관리되고 있다는 사실은 가볍게 볼 문제가 아니다.  #사이버보안 #AI에이전트 #정보보안

(3/6) 이 위험은 단순한 가능성이 아니었습니다. 국정원은 북한이 2년 동안 8차례 선관위를 해킹했다고 통보했지만, 2023년 5월 선관위는 북한발 해킹과 악성코드 수신이 없었다고 다시 거짓말을 했습니다. 선관위 직원의 PC가 북한 김수키 조직의 악성코드에 감염되어 대외비 자료가 유출된 사실이 언론을 통해 드러났습니다. 하지만 국정원 3차장은 감염된 PC가 포맷되거나 반납되어, 어떤 피해가 어디까지 퍼졌는지는 알 수 없다고 증언했습니다.   선관위 서버들은 ‘12345’ 같은 쉬운 비밀번호로 방치되어 있었고, 6,400대의 장비를 지키는 보안 인력은 두세 명에 불과했습니다. 국정원 3차장은 그 인원으로 전산장비를 통제하는 것은 사실상 불가능하다고 했습니다. 그리고 점검하지 못한 나머지 95%의 장비에 대해, 점검한 5%에서 드러난 문제점보다 더해지지 않겠냐고 했습니다. 또한 선관위는 법이 지정한 전문업체가 아닌 곳에 보안 평가를 맡기고 있었습니다.   선관위의 보안이 이렇게 최악의 상태니, 국정원 3차장은 외부 해커나 비인가자가 선관위 시스템을 마비시키거나 파괴하는 것이 가장 두렵다고 했습니다. 재판장님, 적은 이미 문 안에 들어와 있었습니다. 그리고 그 적이 어디까지 다녀갔는지, 지금은 아무도 알 수 없습니다. 2026년 상반기 선관위에 대한 해킹 공격은 10만건을 돌파했으며, 북한의 선관위에 대한 사이버 공격은 올해 상반기 무려 3,543건에 달합니다.   국정원은 선관위에 총선 전까지 조치해 재점검하고, 물리적으로 망을 분리하라고 권고했습니다. 하지만 2024년 1월 국정원의 이행점검 결과, 인터넷망, 업무망과 선거망, 재외선거망까지 물리적 망분리는 미조치로 남아 중장기 과제로 미뤄졌습니다. 사전투표소와 개표소에서 비인가 장비로 선거망에 침투하는 경로도 미조치였습니다. 선거인명부 해킹과 투표지분류기 해킹은 조치 미흡이었습니다. 비밀번호 변경은 직원의 인터뷰로만 확인되어 실제 변경되었는지는 확인할 수 없었습니다. 2025년 국정감사에서 선관위 사무총장은, 사전투표 이틀 동안은 망이 분리되지 않는다고 답했습니다.   선거 시스템 보안의 핵심인 ‘망분리, 비밀번호와 계정, 비인가장비에 대한 접근제어’ 그 어느 것도 개선되지 않았던 것입니다.   헌법 제66조는 대통령에게 국가의 계속성과 헌법을 수호할 책무를 지웁니다. 헌법의 심장은 국민주권이며, 국민주권을 실현하는 통로가 선거입니다. 따라서 헌법수호의 책무는 곧 선거 시스템이라는 국가의 운영체계를 지켜내야 하는 책무와도 같습니다. 확인할 수 없는 개선, 받아들여질지 알 수 없는 재점검, 하지만 윤석열 대통령은 국민의 주권을 지키는 핵심 보안사항을 점검하는 헌법상 의무를 외면하지 않았습니다.   미국의 제20대 대통령 제임스 가필드는 취임연설에서 말했습니다. “선거권의 자유와 신성함을 침해하는 것은 해악 이상의 것입니다. 그것은 범죄이며, 정부 자체를 파괴할 것입니다. 다른 나라에서 왕의 죽음을 꾀하는 것이 대역죄라면, 이 나라에서는 우리의 주권을 목 조르고 주권의 목소리를 막는 것이 그에 못지않은 범죄입니다.”   재판장님, 주권의 목을 조르고 주권의 목소리를 막는 것은 무엇입니까. 바로 국민의 표가 왜곡되거나 조작될 수 있는 상태를 알면서도 아무것도 하지 않는 것입니다. 그 보고를 받고도 침묵한 대통령이 있었다면, 역사는 그를 헌법수호 의무를 저버린 대통령, 가필드의 말처럼 주권의 목소리를 외면한 대역죄로 기록했을 것입니다.   특검은 최후 논고에서 윤석열 대통령의 비상계엄을 '최고 수준의 반역 행위'라고 했습니다. 재판장님, 가필드 대통령이 무엇을 ‘대역죄’에 견주었는지 다시 살펴주십시오. 주권의 목을 조르고 그 목소리를 막는 것이었습니다. 국민의 표가 바뀔 수 있는 문이 열려 있었고, 업무망으로 북한의 해킹 조직이 침투한 사실이 있습니다. 그런데 국가의 가장 중요한 선관위 시스템에 들어온 적을 확인했기에, 개선 여부를 점검하려 한 대통령이 어떻게 반역자가 될 수 있습니까. 반역이라는 말은 나라를 배신하고 적의 편에 선 자에게 쓰는 말입니다. 오히려 국민주권을 바로 세우기 위한 점검을 내란이라 규정하며, 주권의 목을 조르고 있는 특검이 적에게 동조한 대역죄일 것입니다.

Molto poca nella minaccia reale, tantissima nella narrazione:  serve a giustificare i miliardi inviati a Kiev e a vendere l'idea che l'Italia sia sotto assedio diretto di Putin, trasformando un banale doxing da sottobosco Telegram in un atto di guerra esistenziale).   L’eroismo a buon mercato fa sempre comodo quando bisogna convincere i cittadini che la linea bellica non si tocca: basta una provocazione online per trasformare un ministro in un baluardo della democrazia occidentale.   L’ironia, quanto serve. La retorica, purtroppo, abbonda.

CYBERCRIME TIMELINE: COUNTRY-TO-COUNTRY ACTIVITY, 1–8 NOV 2026  Prepared 8 Nov 2026 from Radarwire (GDELT-based news-event data) and open-source reporting. Read the disclaimer at the end before relying on any attribution.  KEY JUDGMENTS  By country flow, suspected Russian activity against Europe (the fridge and blood-bank attacks, the Italy leak) caused the week's highest physical and economic damage, and suspected Russian activity against Ukraine (the Air Alert app, the Kyiv Independent) was information warfare with low-to-moderate damage. Ukraine's hack of Russia's emergency app was retaliation of similar scale. An unidentified criminal actor targeted France for profit, with the largest financial loss. China's Volt Typhoon, exposed this week, is a latent espionage risk against the US and allies rather than a realised loss.  Attribution is weak almost everywhere: only Ukraine's hack of Russia's app is confirmed by a government. Across incidents, intent skews toward psychological pressure and signalling rather than data theft, and physical-world effects such as food spoilage and risk to blood storage are the escalation to watch.  TIMELINE (ALL TIMES APPROXIMATE, UTC UNLESS NOTED)  1 Nov (about 22:47 Kyiv) – suspected Russia against Ukraine. Ukraine's official Air Alert app was hacked and pushed fake radiation, chemical and street-fighting warnings, plus a Russian-language "nuclear alert / Oreshnik is coming" message. It came just as a six-day Kherson ceasefire ended. The likely intent was a psychological operation to cause panic and erode trust. The app was suspended temporarily, there was little sign of panic, and some sirens in the Lviv region reportedly sounded a radiation signal. Attribution confidence is low to medium: Ukraine's Air Force blamed Russia, and a Russia-linked Telegram channel said a group called "Hitcore" claimed it, which is unverified.  2 Nov (about 02:45 Moscow) – Ukraine-linked actors against Russia. Russia's Emergencies Ministry app was hacked and sent a fake "nuclear warheads launched" alert to 33 of 89 regions, also via its channels on the MAX messenger. This looks like retaliation and a mirror-image psychological operation. The app was down about 90 minutes, and the ministry says the national alert system was unaffected. Attribution confidence is high: Zelensky confirmed Ukrainian hackers did it in response to the Air Alert hack (Meduza/PBS), and the group Atesh also posted a screenshot.  1–3 Nov (peak night 1–2 Nov, follow-on 3 Nov) – suspected Russia against EU states. Supermarket refrigeration controllers (Danfoss AK-SM managers) were forced into defrost, with temperatures reportedly reaching 50°C, across Belgium, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Sweden, Estonia, Ireland, Finland, Denmark, Germany, Italy, Romania and Portugal; France had been hit weeks earlier. Three French EFS blood-bank cold stores were also hit through a refrigeration supplier. The likely intent was disruption, signalling capability and sowing public anxiety; there was no ransom demand. Damage was mass food write-offs (for example, SuperValu Ireland pulled stock from 13 stores). Blood supplies were reported unaffected because monitoring caught the temperature spike, and the EU Commission held two crisis meetings. Attribution confidence is low to medium: security firm Lupovis logged reconnaissance from 20–30 Oct (276 attempts by 91 actors, seen only on European sensors), two groups linked to Russian military intelligence reportedly claimed it and then deleted their claims, and the Kremlin denied involvement on 5 Nov. EU wording was divided between "cyberattack" and "incident".  3–4 Nov – unattributed actor against France. Crédit Mutuel Arkéa was hit by fraudulent transfers made from the bank's own account via a third-party provider's platform, with funds reportedly converted to crypto and traced by ZachXBT. The bank disclosed it on 4 Nov. The intent was financial gain. The loss was about €100M (reports up to €118M); the bank says customer funds were untouched and group finances are not threatened, and it notified the ECB, supervisors and prosecutors. There is no attribution, and it looks criminal with no reported state link.  4 Nov – suspected Russia against Ukraine. The Kyiv Independent's website content system and newsletter service were breached, and fake emails and posts claimed a nuclear strike and carried fake Zelensky claims. The likely intent was disinformation and intimidation of independent media. The site was disrupted and fake mail went to subscribers (the outlet has about 3M monthly readers). Attribution confidence is low: it rests on message content, with no technical evidence published, though the pattern resembles the Air Alert incident.  6 Nov – China against the US and allies (disclosure). Lumen's Black Lotus Labs published detail on Volt Typhoon's "Silent Train" covert network of compromised devices and rented infrastructure. The intent is espionage and pre-positioning in telecom and critical infrastructure. No new victim loss was reported; this is exposure of existing access. Confidence on the actor is medium to high, per vendor research.  7 Nov – pro-Russian hackers against Italy. Prime Minister Meloni blamed pro-Russian hackers for leaking Foreign Minister Tajani's personal data on the dark web, per AP/NBC headlines; I could not retrieve the full text. The likely intent is intimidation and political pressure over Italy's Ukraine support. Personal data was exposed, but the scale is not confirmed. Confidence is medium, as it rests on a government statement.  Just outside the window, on 28 Oct, the US Treasury sanctioned North Korean IT-worker facilitators in North Korea, Russia and a Chinese front company. That is state-revenue cybercrime, not a new attack this week.  RADARWIRE "HEAT" AT THE TIME OF EACH ACTIVITY  1–3 Nov, Ukraine–Russia escalation. The 7-day Russia→Ukraine event count was 2,560, versus 721 in the prior window. Radarwire's "Emergency apps hacked in Ukraine and Russia" cluster (2 Nov) coded as a threat event with Goldstein −7.0 and about 60 articles, and "Zelensky concedes counterattack" coverage followed on 3 Nov. The backdrop was planned Ukraine–Russia–US talks and US midterm results shifting Kremlin expectations.  2–7 Nov, fridge attacks. Cyber and infrastructure themes made up 13.1% of global coverage over 7 days (about 262k documents, slightly down on the prior period). By 7 Nov, Radarwire clustered Croatian coverage of the attacks ("password was 12345") as a Russia-threat event, Goldstein −7.0.  3–5 Nov, France. The Arkéa heist coincided with France's nationwide union strikes (hundreds of thousands marched on 5 Nov, and Radarwire flags France as "elevated"), so the bank story competed with domestic unrest for attention.  7–8 Nov, Poland. The Kraków market-square shooting (six killed; attacker described as ultranationalist) became the top-trending story globally, with 150+ outlets in 12 hours, and Poland is "elevated" against its norm. Poland also tightened its Kaliningrad border amid reported Russian sabotage concerns. Cyber stories lost attention share to this on 7–8 Nov.  Iran and Israel. US↔Iran and Israel→Iran remain among the heaviest conflict dyads (US→Iran 445 events, Israel→Iran 180 in 7 days). The 2026 Iran war has a documented cyber dimension, but I verified no specific Iran-related cyber incident inside this window.  WHAT TO WATCH NEXT  Watch for any official EU or national attribution of the fridge attacks, and for a second wave against hospitals, data centres or other building-management systems. Also watch whether Ukraine–Russia alert-app attacks recur around the planned talks, how much of the Arkéa money is recovered and whether it links to known crypto-laundering clusters, and whether NoName057(16)-style pressure continues against Italy and other Ukraine supporters.  LIMITS OF THIS REPORT  Radarwire's event search matches actor names only, so cyber incidents were identified from its news clusters and confirmed through open-source reporting. Counts of affected countries differ by source (9 per Euronews, 12 per RetailDetail). I excluded brief mentions I could not verify: the parliament of Ecuador, a Taiwan bank, a Brazilian health department and a German hosting provider.  DISCLAIMER  This report is an informational summary compiled from machine-coded news data (Radarwire/GDELT) and publicly available media and vendor reports as of 8 Nov 2026. It is not intelligence, legal, financial or security advice. Event data are automatically extracted and may contain errors, duplicates or misattributions. Attribution of cyber incidents is inherently uncertain: statements that a state or group was behind an attack are allegations, claims or assessments unless a government or court has confirmed them, and claims by hacker groups are often exaggerated, retracted or false. Statements of intent and damage are analytic judgments, not established facts, and figures (such as financial losses) are reported estimates that may change. Nothing here should be read as accusing any government, organisation or person of wrongdoing. Details were accurate to the best of my knowledge at the time of writing, are fast-moving, and should be checked against primary sources (national CERTs, ENISA, company statements) before use in decisions. sample_tweets.text: 🚨 Security researcher hacks Meta Ray-Ban smart glasses, achieves arbitrary code execution  A security researcher has demonstrated how vulnerabilities in Meta's Ray-Ban smart glasses allowed the installation of unauthorized applications and execution of arbitrary code directly on the device.  The researcher discovered that firmware version 126 and earlier failed to verify application signatures, allowing a modified Android APK to run on the glasses and provide interactive shell access over Wi-Fi Direct.  Although Meta introduced signature verification in firmware 127, the researcher bypassed the protection by manipulating a configuration file delivered through the paired smartphone.  The findings were reported to Meta through its bug bounty program, and the company approved public disclosure. The researcher believes the issues have since been fixed, although that has not been independently confirmed.

Under those conditions, attacker-controlled session data can be interpreted as a serialized PHP object.  PHP Sessions | Object Injection / RCE:  CVSS: 8.1 High Attack: Remote, unauthenticated Preconditions: Specific serializer mismatch + session upload progress enabled Mitigation: Set session.upload_progress.enabled=0 in server configuration and restart PHP workers  The PoC demonstrates the full session upload-progress chain and shows how object injection can become code execution when a usable gadget class is present in the target application.

When I think of highly effective autonomous attacks, I don't think of anything from the AI era. I think of Emotet. I'd argue it was the pinnacle of sophistication for at-scale financially-motivated malware operations.  The malware lands on a corporate endpoint, immediately exfiltrates the victim's SMTP (email) credentials, as well as their email inbox. Their inbox gets sent to the  threat actor's backend processing pipeline, which scrapes the victim's inbox for email threads where the last reply was by someone other than the victim.  The pipeline then crafts a reply to the email thread containing a backdoored Microsoft Office document, which is usually presented as an invoice or something time-sensitive that the target is likely to open. The emails were then farmed out to the infected systems, and sent using legitimate stolen SMTP credentials.  The use of legit credentials + corporate systems as spam bots bypassed SPF / DKIM, and IP based spam blocklists, ensuring the email was highly likely to land in the target's inbox, not get blocked or sent to spam.  The recipient receives an email from a party they know, trust, have had previous communications with, and is in reply to an existing email exchange between the target and victim. Basically email worm meets extremely effective spearphishing at scale.  They say you don't gotta hand it to them, but you kinda do. The engineering that went into this botnet's infrastructure was incredible. The pipeline had a polymorphic engine that would rewrite the malware's code every time antivirus vendors tried to add detections for it. It put plenty of state-sponsored malware operations to shame.  The malware was so effective that 8 different countries banded together to stop it. They hacked into the command-and-control infrastructure, then used the malware's self-update command to push out code that removed the malware from the system and then deletes itself.  It set precedent for governments being able to, in extreme circumstances, mass-hack victim systems and deploy code designed to disinfect said systems. Previously, there was only law enforcement precedent for triggering the malware's built in remove command, displaying warning messages, or simply just seizing / hijacking the control infrastructure.  The botnet had been running for about 12 years when it was taken out in 2021. They just don't make malware like they used to. Everything from the post AI-era is borderline slop and I'm bored out of my mind analyzing it.  The below image is what the Microsoft Office documents the target received would look like. Clicking the "Enable Content" button runs the malware.

The reason these "throw everything at once" style agentic cyberattacks work is because most orgs are chronically terrified of deploying deterministic detection + remediation automations.   Most security products have a "lock out this account" or "disconnect this system" or "block this IP" options that you can set if certain alerts are triggered. But because business function takes precedent, most orgs would rather risk a successful intrusion than an accidental disruption.  There's no reason to believe that "agentic defenders" would be a viable solution. Defenders need to consume many times more context/signals that attackers do, therefore by nature are slower. Defenders win on controlling the playing field, not out-maneuvering attackers like it's some Hollywood style fighter jet battle.  In the same way that reactive human defenses are slower than human offense, reactive AI defense are slower than AI offense (and regular old deterministic automations, too). The whole "fight AI with AI" thing is pretty ridiculous and misunderstands what good defense looks like.  The only answer is proactive defense + fast deterministic detection & response. But nobody is ready for that talk yet, so we're probably just gonna do like 10 years of "agentic AI SOC", until everyone runs out of money and/or figures out it doesn't work.

*   **Storm-2603**: SharePoint 취약점을 악용한 파일리스(Fileless) 공격을 수행하며, ToolShell을 활용해 시스템 내부로 침투([Securelist](https://securelist.com/storm-2603-fileless-toolshell-attack/121467/)).
